neighbours.label: unclear: 'to' after a willingness predicate ('willing to', 'ready to')
fire: Before you negotiate, decide how far you are willing to bend.
Few of the donors were willing to give more than last year.
She asked whether anyone was willing to cover the night shift.
The landlord seemed willing to lower the rent a little.
Are you prepared to take the risk if the market falls?
He was never willing to admit that he had been wrong.
Most voters are unwilling to pay higher taxes for roads.
The team is ready to take on the champions next week.
quiet: Before you negotiate, decide what your lowest price will be.
Few of the donors gave more than they did last year.
She asked whether anyone had covered the night shift.
The landlord lowered the rent a little in the spring.
Do you know the risk if the market falls next month?
He never admitted that he had been wrong about it.
Most voters pay higher taxes than they did ten years ago.
The team plays against the champions next week.
